description: Two-panel line-chart figure presenting statistics on intragranular κ-carbides in Nb-containing medium-Mn low-density steels, both panels over an identical categorical x-axis labelled "Samples" with four conditions: as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h. Panel (a) plots "Average size (nm)" (y-axis 0–10, gridlines every 2) and every data point carries an error bar; panel (b) plots "Volume fraction (vol.%)" (y-axis 0–30, gridlines every 5) with no visible error bars. Both panels share the same legend: "0.02Nb steels" as dark-grey squares and "0.04Nb steels" as red circles. In both panels the curves increase monotonically with aging temperature, and the 0.02Nb curve lies above the 0.04Nb curve at every condition. At 823 K/3 h the 0.02Nb points lie just below the 8 nm and 30 vol.% gridlines, whereas the 0.04Nb points reach roughly the 6.4 nm level and just above the 20 vol.% gridline. The figure demonstrates that aging increases both the size and the volume fraction of κ-carbides, that a higher aging temperature gives a greater increase, and that the higher-Nb steel consistently precipitates fewer and smaller κ-carbides.

subfigures.description: Line plot of average κ-carbide size (nm; y-axis 0–10, gridlines every 2) versus sample condition (as-cast, 723 K/3 h, 773 K/3 h, 823 K/3 h). Two curves with error bars: 0.02Nb steels (dark-grey squares) and 0.04Nb steels (red circles). Both curve upwards with increasing aging temperature; the 0.02Nb curve is above the 0.04Nb curve at every condition and ends just below the 8 nm gridline, the 0.04Nb curve ending near the 6.4 nm level.

Line plot of κ-carbide volume fraction (vol.%; y-axis 0–30, gridlines every 5) versus the same four sample conditions, with the same colour/symbol legend (0.02Nb dark squares, 0.04Nb red circles) and no discernible error bars. Both curves rise monotonically; 0.02Nb remains above 0.04Nb, ending just below the 30 vol.% gridline, while the 0.04Nb curve ends just above the 20 vol.% gridline.

observations.observation: The figure consists of two stacked line charts: (a) plots 'Average size (nm)' on a 0–10 y-axis and (b) plots 'Volume fraction (vol.%)' on a 0–30 y-axis.
Both panels use the identical categorical x-axis labelled 'Samples' with four entries printed as 'as-cast', '723 K/3 h', '773 K/3 h' and '823 K/3 h'.
Both panels carry the same legend: '0.02Nb steels' drawn as dark-grey squares and '0.04Nb steels' drawn as red circles.
In panel (a) every plotted point has an error bar; in panel (b) no error bars are discernible.

In panel (a) both curves rise monotonically with aging temperature and the 0.02Nb curve lies above the 0.04Nb curve at every one of the four conditions; at 823 K/3 h the 0.02Nb point sits just below the 8 nm gridline while the 0.04Nb point sits near the 6.4 nm level.

In panel (b) both curves rise monotonically with aging temperature, the 0.02Nb curve always above the 0.04Nb curve; at 823 K/3 h the 0.02Nb point lies just below the 30 vol.% gridline while the 0.04Nb point lies just above the 20 vol.% gridline.
The caption states that after aging at 823 K the volume fraction of κ-carbides in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels increases from 3.3 and 1.6 vol% in the as-cast state to 27.8 and 26.7 vol%, respectively.

Discrepancy: the caption's 26.7 vol% for 0.04Nb at 823 K is not supported by the pixels, where the red 0.04Nb point at 823 K/3 h lies only just above the 20 vol.% gridline (the 27.8 vol% value for 0.02Nb does match its plotted point just below the 30 gridline).
The caption states the average κ-carbide size in 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels increases from 2.0 and 1.9 nm (as-cast) to 7.8 and 6.4 nm at 823 K.
The citing text states that κ-carbides in 0.04Nb steels consistently have a smaller content and size than those in 0.02Nb steels, as plotted in Figure 7.
The caption identifies the figure as reporting the average size (a) and volume fraction (b) of κ-carbides in the Nb-containing steels.
The citing text states that the Figure 7 data were combined with Eq. (8) to calculate precipitation strengthening of 59.4 MPa for the as-cast 0.02Nb steel and 180.6 MPa after aging at 723 K.
